_readme.purpose: Grammar-first parser spec for the clearance-state runway monitor. Match these BEFORE asking any language model; the model only handles residue and must emit the same event schema with a confidence. Canonical forms are quoted from FAA JO 7110.65BB chapter 3 (sections 1, 7, 9, 10) as fetched Oct 2, 2026; 'as_heard' variants come from the LaGuardia 2026-03-22 captions and the Logan 2026-06-20 NTSB table.
pipeline: 1 normalize: spoken numbers → digits (niner→9, tree→3, fife→5, 'one three'→13, 'two two'→22, 'four'→4, 'one three left'→13L); ICAO phonetics → letters (alpha→A, 'alpha alpha'/'double alpha'→AA, 'golf golf'→GG); strip fillers (uh, um, okay, roger when not a readback)

2 identify speaker/callsign: airline telephony + flight number; N-number; vehicle ('Truck 1 and company', 'Ops 2'); 'LaGuardia Tower'/'Ground' addressed = pilot/vehicle transmission; trailing callsign = readback/report
3 match patterns in priority order below; first full match wins; partial match → emit with lower confidence and missing slots = null
4 never fill a hold_short or runway slot that was not heard; null is a first-class value (acknowledged=UNKNOWN downstream)

patterns.cite: 3-7-2 PHRASEOLOGY: RUNWAY (number), TAXI VIA (route as necessary) … HOLD SHORT OF (location)
as_heard: Runway 13, November, Alpha, and Echo, hold short runway 4
Runway 13, taxi via Mike, Bravo, Papa, hold short runway 22
patterns.notes: The route is the segment list the engine traces on the graph. If the traced route crosses a runway and no hold_short names it → rule R6 'missing hold'.

patterns.cite: non-standard but routine turn instructions (LGA 2026-03-22: 'make the right turn at Lima and a left turn on Bravo'; 'make it Bravo, short of November')
3-7-2 PHRASEOLOGY: HOLD SHORT OF (location); HOLD POSITION
as_heard: hold short of Mike
once you join Bravo, hold short of Lima
hold your position

patterns.cite: 3-7-2 PHRASEOLOGY: CROSS (runway) AT (runway/taxiway). 'Issue a crossing clearance to vehicles for each runway their route crosses.' 'An aircraft must have crossed a previous runway before another runway crossing clearance may be issued.'
as_heard: Truck 1 and company, cross 4 at Delta
patterns.notes: Engine: reserve <runway> for <callsign> as CROSSING at <at>; start the 'close out the crossing' timer; §3-1-3 means local approval is implied when ground issues it.

patterns.cite: vehicle/pilot request (LGA: 'Truck 1 and company, LaGuardia Tower, requesting to cross 4 at Delta')
§3-1-3: 'The ground controller must advise the local controller when the coordinated runway operation is complete.' Pilot/vehicle form: 'clear of runway (number)' / 'across (number)'
3-9-4 PHRASEOLOGY: RUNWAY (number), LINE UP AND WAIT (+ traffic advisory: 'traffic holding in position' / 'traffic landing')
as_heard: American 3161, runway 27, line up and wait, traffic landing runway 33L

patterns.regex: RUNWAY (?P<runway>\d{1,2}[LRC]?)[,]? CLEARED FOR TAKEOFF(?P<adv>.*)?|(?P<adv2>TRAFFIC [^,]+),? RUNWAY (?P<runway2>\d{1,2}[LRC]?)[,]? CLEARED FOR TAKEOFF
as_heard: United 2384, traffic inside three mile final runway 4, runway 13, cleared for takeoff
2384, wind 070 at 5, runway 13, cleared for takeoff
patterns.notes: Advisory text present → the intersecting-runway rule downgrades to ADVISED (LGA negative case).

patterns.cite: 3-9-10: CANCEL TAKEOFF CLEARANCE (reason); and any STOP instruction
as_heard: Truck 1, stop, stop, stop
Frontier 4195, just stop there please
patterns.notes: Engine: mark the addressed entity's authorization CANCELLED-UNACKNOWLEDGED until a readback/report; keep the reservation (the runway is not free until an observed/reported state says so).

patterns.cite: 3-10-5 PHRASEOLOGY: RUNWAY (number), CLEARED TO LAND (+ 'number (N)', 'traffic holding in position', anticipated-separation advisory)
patterns.regex: RUNWAY (?P<runway>\d{1,2}[LRC]?)[,]? CLEARED TO LAND(?:[, ]*NUMBER (?P<seq>\w+))?(?P<adv>.*)?|CLEARED TO LAND (?:RUNWAY )?(?P<runway2>\d{1,2}[LRC]?)(?:[, ]*NUMBER (?P<seq2>\w+))?
as_heard: Runway 4, cleared to land, number two, Jazz 646
Delta 2351, runway 33L, cleared to land, traffic holding on runway 27
Delta 263, go around, runway heading, 2000
Delta 2351 is going around
patterns.notes: Releases the LANDING reservation for the addressed callsign.

patterns.regex: HOLDING SHORT (?:OF )?(?:RUNWAY )?(?P<hold>\d{1,2}[LRC]?|[A-Z]{1,2})|(?:IS |WE'RE )?ON (?P<twy>[A-Z]{1,2})\b|READY TO TAXI|REJECT(?:ED|ING)|ABORT(?:ED|ING)|DECLARING AN EMERGENCY|REQUEST(?:ING)? FIRE
as_heard: Ground, 2384 is on Bravo
United 2384 is rejecting on 13
2384 is declaring an emergency
patterns.notes: 'rejected on 13' → the aircraft is OCCUPYING runway 13 until an exit instruction and report.

patterns.cite: 3-7-2: 'Request a read back of runway hold short instructions when it is not received' → the engine treats a readback that omits the hold-short as NOT acknowledged
patterns.rule: A pilot/vehicle transmission that follows an ATC instruction to the same callsign within 15 s and repeats ≥1 slot is a READBACK. Compare slot by slot: runway, route, hold_short, crossing_at. Missing hold_short → acknowledged.hold_short=UNKNOWN; different runway → DISCREPANT.
as_heard: Runway 13, November, Alpha, Echo, hold short runway 4, United 2384 (complete)
Bravo short of Lima, let you know, 2384 (complete, abbreviated)
Runway 13, Alpha, Delta, ho— (clipped → hold_short null)

patterns.notes: Keeps the entity's state; changes which lane later transmissions are expected on.

patterns.cite: 3-7-2 vehicle phraseology: PROCEED / CROSS / HOLD SHORT

callsign_patterns.abbreviated: trailing or leading flight number only ('2384', '234' for United 2384 — the LGA controller clipped it to '234' twice); resolve by most-recent same-prefix callsign on frequency, confidence ≤ 0.7
callsign_patterns.lookalike_guard: flag two active callsigns differing by one digit or one phonetic (e.g., 2384/2348, 4195/4159) — Addendum 6 idea 13

asr_repairs_observed.note: Errors seen in the public captions of the LGA audio; a grammar that expects HOLD SHORT OF (taxiway) repairs each.
pairs: hold your text to wake Kila
